text:
In the valley of Oropher, lived a cartographer named Elias. He possessed the finest maps ever inked, capturing every contour with mathematical perfection. To Elias, the world was not made of soil and stone, but of lines and labels.

One autumn, a traveler sought the hidden lake of Mirra. Elias consulted his parchment, pointing to a blue stain labeled "Lake." "Follow this line," he commanded, confident in its geometry. The traveler walked until the path vanished into dense, thorny undergrowth. There was no water, only mud and mosquitoes.

Furious, the traveler returned. "Your map is a lie!" he shouted.

Elias smiled serenely. "The map is true. It shows what *should* be there, based on last year’s survey. The country merely failed to comply."

He never ventured outside his study again, trusting his paper world more than the living one. When drought struck, his maps showed rivers where dust lay dry. He starved while clutching a perfect picture of plenty, blind to the fact that a drawing of bread cannot fill an empty belly.
